title: Bram and the Choir
premise: Cyrus Vane, a cartographer of unmapped realms, has spent her life in the valley where magic cannot follow, hiding the gift that lets her chart places that do not yet exist. When the crown's witch-hunters arrive seeking anyone with the gift, Cyrus flees with Bram, a mute choirboy whose voice was sold to the court beneath the mountain to pay his family's debts. Guided by her impossible maps, she descends into the unmapped dark to steal his soul back from the Choir—a chorus of stolen voices that sings the mountain kingdom into being. In the end Cyrus learns she herself is the final note the Choir lacks, and she must choose between trading her own soul for Bram's or shattering the Choir entirely, an act that unmakes the court but frees every stolen voice—including, at last, her mother's.
about_author: Ines Kavanagh is the pen name of a former choir singer turned archivist who grew up in a mining town ringed by mountains. She writes fantasy about borrowed voices, buried bargains, and the maps people draw to find their way home.

chapters.title: The Valley That Refuses Magic
chapters.summary: Cyrus Vane's POV. Cyrus finishes a map of a city that will not exist for fifty years, then hides it beneath her floorboards as crown riders enter the valley. The beat is quiet dread: her sanctuary has never been safe, only unnoticed.

chapters.title: A Boy Who Cannot Sing
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. At market she notices Bram, a choirboy who mouths hymns without sound, and recognizes the hollow look of someone missing a piece of themselves. His grandmother begs her to read a contract written on skin. Beat: reluctant compassion kindling.

chapters.title: The Proclamation
chapters.summary: Bram's POV, rendered through his silent observations. The magistrate reads the crown's decree: all gifted persons must surrender for 'assessment.' Bram watches Cyrus's face as she realizes the hunt is for her. Beat: fear becoming resolve.

chapters.title: What the Contract Cost
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. She deciphers the soul-contract: Bram's voice sold to the court beneath the mountain, payment due in full by midwinter or his whole family follows. Beat: guilt—her maps once guided the debt-collectors' road here.

chapters.title: Leaving the Valley
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Cyrus and Bram slip past the warding stones at night; magic floods back into Cyrus like cold water, and her gift ignites uncontrollably. Beat: exhilaration shadowed by terror at what she can now do—and what it reveals.

chapters.title: The Road of Borrowed Names
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Traveling under false names, they shelter with a hedge-witch who recognizes Cyrus's gift and warns that the crown's hunters carry compasses that point at talent. Beat: first taste of found-friendship and its fragility.

chapters.title: Hunters at the Ford
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Witch-hunters corner them at a river crossing; Cyrus's panicked gift floods the valley with phantom roads, confusing even the hunters' compasses. They escape, but she collapses. Beat: her power is both shield and wound.

chapters.title: The Map That Draws Itself
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Her blood, spilled at the ford, seeps into parchment and charts the true road beneath the mountain—impossible, alive, hungry. Beat: awe curdling into suspicion about where her gift actually comes from.

chapters.title: The Village That Forgot Its Name
chapters.summary: Dual POV. They pass a village emptied of memory, its names scraped off gravestones—the Choir's leavings. An old woman hums fragments of songs no one taught her. Beat: horror at the scale of what stole Bram's voice.

chapters.title: The First Door Beneath
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Following her living map, they find a door in a cliff face that opens only to a sung note—which Bram cannot give. Cyrus fakes the pitch with her gift. Beat: teamwork, and the door remembering her voice too well.

chapters.title: Stairs Made of Silence
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Descending, Bram hears echoes of his own voice calling from the walls, taunting him home. He nearly turns back; Cyrus refuses to leave him. Beat: despair met with stubborn loyalty.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. They reach a cathedral cavern lit by hanging lanterns of trapped breath, ruled by the Maestro, a courteous, terrible figure who greets Cyrus as 'the cartographer we have waited for.' Beat: the trap closes gently.

chapters.title: An Audience of Voices
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The Maestro offers a bargain: Bram's soul for Cyrus's services mapping new realms for the expanding court. Cyrus pretends to consider. Beat: moral vertigo—survival offered at another's expense.

chapters.title: The Choir Revealed
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Shown the Choir: hundreds of stolen souls singing the kingdom's borders into permanence, including, Cyrus realizes with horror, a voice that harmonizes like her mother's. Beat: grief detonating into purpose.

chapters.title: The Price of Survival
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Cyrus discovers the truth of her inheritance: her gift is a Choir fragment, seeded in her bloodline so the court could always reclaim it. Her mother didn't flee—she was harvested. Beat: identity shattered and reformed.

chapters.title: A Bargain in the Dark
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Locked in guest chambers, Cyrus and Bram plan betrayal; Bram, voiceless, communicates through the hymn-rhythms he taps, teaching her the Choir's structure. Beat: intimacy forged in shared defiance.

chapters.title: The False Note
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. During the coronation concert, Cyrus slips among the Choir and plants a discord using her gift, bending one stolen voice against the others. The mountain shudders. Beat: sabotage, and no way back.

chapters.title: What the Song Unmade
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. The discord spreads; the court's halls unravel into raw stone as the Choir fractures. The Maestro hunts them through collapsing galleries, offering Cyrus her mother's voice if she restores the song. Beat: temptation at knife-point.

chapters.title: The Final Note
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Cornered above the abyss, Cyrus understands the Maestro needs her as the Choir's keystone. Instead she pours her entire gift into one note—not joining the song, but ending it. Beat: sacrificial climax.

chapters.title: Every Voice Released
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The Choir breaks; souls stream upward like migrating birds. Bram's voice returns mid-scream, then mid-laugh. Her mother's presence brushes Cyrus once—forgiveness, not farewell—before departing. Beat: catharsis and cost.

chapters.title: The Unmapped Country
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Giftless now, Cyrus climbs toward daylight beside Bram, who sings the old valley hymns to guide her steps. The crown's hunt collapses with the court's evidence buried. Beat: quiet grief braided with freedom.

chapters.title: Bram and the Choir
chapters.summary: Epilogue, dual POV. A year later, Cyrus draws ordinary maps in the valley while Bram rebuilds its choir around freed voices who wandered home. On her desk, a blank page begins, faintly, to chart itself. Beat: hope with a door left open.
